decision: Finish only when bootstrap, shared query policy, all cache-safe direct web reads behind Query (gate: 95 adapter reads, 26 intentional imperative, 1 pairing), theme catalog domain wired through the same transport and mounted in settings Appearance, settings-boundary e2e regressions fixed, behavior tests, visual proof, APK, and release checks pass
why: This turns the migration into a falsifiable product and repository predicate instead of a dependency-install task
evidence: docs/specs/server-state-query-migration.md, bun scripts/check-query-migration.mjs (95/26/1), frontend/src/lib/query/themes.ts, frontend/src/routes/settings/+page.svelte Appearance tab

decision: Adopt TanStack Query for cache-safe server state on web and mobile, with an in-memory cache and no offline mutation replay
why: The repeated page waterfalls come from independently owned remote reads and loading states; one query owner can deduplicate reads, preserve cached data, and share policy without persisting sensitive data

decision: Keep generated OpenAPI types and framework-neutral query definitions in separate workspace packages
why: The contract should remain generated and authoritative while query keys, policy, normalization, retry, cancellation, and invalidation stay reusable across Svelte and React

decision: Add one optional-auth application bootstrap read
why: A single startup read removes the auth, Workspace, and settings waterfall without breaking older endpoints or requiring a database migration

decision: Partition every Workspace query key and clear the whole cache only when actor, server, or token identity changes
why: Workspace switches may retain safely isolated cached data; identity switches must never expose the previous actor's state

decision: Delay cold first-viewport placeholders by 150 ms and keep cached content visible during refresh
why: Fast reads should not flash skeletons; slow reads need one content-shaped page boundary; background work must not replace usable content

decision: Implement the additive bootstrap endpoint and strict optional-auth failure classification
why: The web and mobile startup paths need one response while outages and database failures must not be misreported as anonymous or invalid credentials

decision: Prove Query client policy, session cache clearing, request deduplication, and the Publications Activity pilot before expanding
why: The riskiest shared behavior needs executable evidence before migrating the remaining domains

decision: Use one delayed PageContainer loading boundary while reserving header-action layout
why: This removes short skeleton flashes without layout shift and cancels stale timers when loading resolves or restarts

decision: Keep implementation slices in Worktrunk-managed branches and merge only the fully verified candidate into main
why: Independent commits stay reviewable and revertible while the release task owns main and the shared Devenv lane

decision: Add an AST-based allowlist gate before expanding the web migration
why: The baseline must distinguish the exact 20 intentional one-shot reads, the CLI pairing read, Query adapters, and the excluded Image Editor adapter from 98 cache-safe reads that still bypass Query; every domain slice can now measure the debt it removes

decision: Expose small domain query interfaces with web and mobile transport adapters, and keep key, policy, normalization, retry, cancellation, seeding, and invalidation logic behind those interfaces
why: Web and mobile are two real adapters at one shared seam; domain interfaces avoid one shallow transport wrapper or one giant catalog interface while concentrating behavior and tests
evidence: packages/query-catalog/src (accounts, admin, themes, ... per-domain *QueryAPI + transports; see packages/query-catalog/src/themes.ts and its web adapter frontend/src/lib/query/themes.ts)
